records.title: Subagents inherit the parent's creation-time model seed instead of its live route, delegation silently runs on for exmaple `openrouter/auto` after the default model is switched
records.body:
### Summary

When the configured default model is changed (e.g. from **Auto Router** (`openrouter/auto`) to a concrete model like `stealth/ox-alpha`), sessions that were created — or merely *resumed* — under the old default keep spawning subagents that still route on the old model. The main chat visibly runs the new model, while every delegated child silently answers via the router, which fans out to arbitrary upstream models.

The cause looks like a split-brain between two per-session "model" values: the **request route** (what the chat actually sends on) and the **agent seed options** (stamped at create/resume time). Subagent delegation reads the latter.

### Environment

- DeepSeek Harness desktop packaging, `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.1-rc.2 (`dsh-subagent`, `dsh-host-apiproxy`, `dsh-agent-default-model` all 0.1.1-rc.2)
- Linux x64 (Fedora, kernel 7.1.9), Web GUI at `127.0.0.1:3081`
- Provider: `openrouter`; default model was at some point set to `openrouter/auto` ("Auto Router"), later switched to `stealth/ox-alpha`

### Evidence

From session logs (`.dsh/sessions/...`):

Parent session — requests actually running Ox Alpha:

```json
{"type":"request/header","data":{"header":{"config":{"provider":"openrouter","model":"stealth/ox-alpha"}}}}
```

…yet every child it spawned around that time carried the stale seed:

```json
{"type":"subagent/descriptor","data":{"version":2,"mode":"continuable","provider":"spawn","label":"Add serverbound play interaction packets","agentProvider":"openrouter","agentModel":"openrouter/auto"}}
```

and the children's own `request/header` events confirm they really called `openrouter/auto`.

### Root cause walkthrough

1. **Web layer seeds options once per create/resume.** In `dsh-host-apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts`:

   ```ts
   /** The seed model each create/resume declares; re-read so it never goes stale. */
   const agentOptions = () => {
       const { provider, model } = defaults.defaultModelSelection();
       return { provider, model };
   };
   ```

   "Never goes stale" only holds *across* create/resume calls. A session left open across a default change keeps the old seed.

2. **Per-session selection is separate and doesn't touch options.** `selectionFor()` resolves the request route as: in-process UI pick → latest logged `request/header` → live `agent-default-model`. Switching models in the UI (or changing the default) updates what the chat sends on — but never rewrites `agent.options`.

3. **Delegation reads the raw seed.** In `packages/subagent/subagent/src/child-agent.ts`:

   ```ts
   export function resolveChildAgentOptions(parent, requested, childDepth): AgentOptions {
     const parentProvider = parent.options.provider
     const parentModel = parent.options.model        // ← stale creation-time seed
     ...
   ```

   The continuable descriptor snapshot in `SubagentRuntime.startContinuable` duplicates the same read:

   ```ts
   const agentProvider = request.agentOptions?.provider ?? parent.options.provider;
   const agentModel = request.agentOptions?.model ?? parent.options.model;
   ```

So a session seeded while the default was `openrouter/auto` keeps delegating children on `openrouter/auto` indefinitely, even while the parent itself runs a concrete model. The same applies to any long-lived session after any default change — the drift is just most visible (and most costly) with a router model, where you don't control which upstream model answers.

### Proposed fix

Make delegation follow the parent's **live** route, falling back to the seed only before the first request exists. The folded request header is already the exact source `selectionFor()` uses for sessions without an in-process pick:

```ts
/**
 * The parent's LIVE route: the request route its session actually last ran on,
 * falling back to creation-time seed options before the first request.
 */
function parentLiveRoute(parent: Agent) {
  const logged = parent.session?.requestHeader?.()?.config
  return {
    provider: logged?.provider ?? parent.options?.provider,
    model: logged?.model ?? parent.options?.model,
  }
}

export function resolveChildAgentOptions(parent, requested, childDepth): AgentOptions {
  const route = parentLiveRoute(parent)
  return {
    ...route.provider !== undefined ? { provider: route.provider } : {},
    ...route.model !== undefined ? { model: route.model } : {},
    ...parent.options.maxTokens !== undefined ? { maxTokens: parent.options.maxTokens } : {},
    ...requested,                       // explicit per-child overrides still win
    subagentDepth: childDepth,
  }
}
```

…and use the same helper for the descriptor snapshot in `startContinuable` (both the bundled copy and `types/child-agent.ts`).

I've been running exactly this patch locally (verified: stale-seed parent with live Ox Alpha route → child gets `stealth/ox-alpha`; blank parent → falls back to seed; per-child override → respected). Happy to open a PR if you tell me which repo/branch to target and whether you'd prefer this shape or a different one.

### Alternative directions

- Re-seed `agent.options` when a session's effective selection changes (keeps inheritance semantics but makes the web layer own the sync), or
- Expose the installed per-session selection on the Agent context so the subagent runtime can query it directly instead of folding the log.

### Workarounds (until fixed)

- Re-open/resume affected sessions after changing the default model (resume re-declares fresh seed options), and/or
- Explicitly pick the desired model in each session's model picker before delegating.

One caveat users should know: since `selectionFor()` prefers the latest logged request over the live default, resuming does *not* reset what an existing session sends on — only what future subagents inherit. Both surfaces have to be checked when chasing "why is my subagent on a different model".

We hit this on `0.1.1-rc.2` as well (Web GUI `dsh web`, `llm-pi-ai` adapter, Windows), using two providers that share the same logical model under different ids. Independent confirmation of the report:

- The parent session ran **100%** of its requests on provider `bitdeer` (`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`), and the parent log contains **zero** references to the stale provider.
- **All 43 subagents** spawned by 6 `workflow` runs (in-process `spawn`, one-shot mode) ran on the stale route `opencode-go` / `deepseek-v4-flash`, and at least one child exhausted that provider's **weekly quota** (`429 GoUsageLimitError`, "Weekly usage limit reached") — so the drift is consequential, not cosmetic.

Representative child `request/header` while the parent's own concurrent requests were bitdeer:

```json
{"type":"request/header","data":{"header":{"config":{"provider":"opencode-go","model":"deepseek-v4-flash","maxTokens":384000}}}}
```

Two small observations that may matter for the fix:

1. Our one-shot `spawn` descriptor (`{"version":2,"mode":"one-shot","provider":"spawn"}`) does **not** carry `agentProvider`/`agentModel` like the continuable descriptor in the report — yet the misroute is identical. So the load-bearing fix is `resolveChildAgentOptions` reading the live route; the descriptor only needs mirroring where it stores the pair. And remember the function exists in **two** copies (`dsh-subagent/lib/index.js` bundled + `lib/types/child-agent.js`) — both must change.
2. Contributing hazard in our setup: provider `A` serves the *namespaced* id `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` while another route (`opencode-go`) owns the *bare* id `deepseek-v4-flash`. We suspect the creation-time seed carried the bare id (the id shared by the base default and that route), which is what made the stale seed land on a specific unintended provider. A warning whenever a request is routed on a bare model id across providers — as suggested in the report — would have surfaced this immediately.

The proposed direction (delegation follows the parent's live route — the folded `requestHeader` — with fallback to the seed only before the first request) matches exactly what we'd expect. We also confirmed the workaround end-to-end: **opening a fresh session after switching the default re-stamps the seed**, so parent and children agree again (with the report's caveat that merely resuming an existing session does not reset its request route — only what future children inherit).

Happy to share sanitized session excerpts or help test the patch against the pi-ai multi-provider adapter.

This stale-seed case now has a verified alternative path through the Pi plugin ecosystem. It does **not** patch DSH native subagents; `pi2dsh` lets stock `@tintinweb/pi-subagents` create native DSH child sessions:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <你的-profile> add pi2dsh
dsh plugin --profile <你的-profile> add @tintinweb/pi-subagents
```

For an unpinned child, route precedence is: explicit Pi child model → the caller session's last durable real `request/header` route → creation-time options only as fallback. Provider and model travel as one pair.

The acceptance test uses stock dsh-TUI and real model calls: the parent first runs on `deepseek-official`, `/model` switches it to an independent `work-gw`, and then it spawns an unpinned child. Assertions read the durable parent/child JSONL rather than UI text: parent routes are `official → work-gw`; child routes contain only `work-gw`; the child also executes a real tool and lands a marker. This specifically falsifies the creation-time-seed failure shape described here.

records.title: BUG: Spawned subagents inherit `agent.options` stamped at agent creation, not the agent's current model selection
records.body:
# Spawned subagents inherit `agent.options` stamped at agent creation, not the agent's current model selection — silent cross-provider divergence after a model switch

## Summary

An agent's **`options` (provider/model/maxTokens) are stamped once at session/agent creation** and are never rewritten when the user changes the model. Per-request model changes are applied by a **separate layer** — the `agent/request` waterfall (`installModelSelection` in `dsh-agent`) — which only overrides the **current agent's own requests** using a live per-session selection.

Subagents, however, inherit the parent's **`options`** (`resolveChildAgentOptions` in `dsh-subagent`) and completely bypass that overrides layer.

Net consequence: after the user switches the session model, the parent's live requests use the **new** model while **every subsequently spawned subagent runs the old model — potentially a different provider with real billing/quota impact** — with no visible sign in the parent session.

Observed in a real session: the parent session ran **100%** of its requests on provider `bitdeer`, while **all 43 subagents** spawned by 6 `workflow` runs ran on provider `opencode-go` / model `deepseek-v4-flash`, exhausting that provider's weekly quota (`429 GoUsageLimitError`). The parent session log contains **zero** references to `opencode-go`.

## Environment

- dsh packages: `0.1.1-rc.2` (`dsh-agent`, `dsh-agent-loop`, `dsh-subagent`, `dsh-workflow-worker-thread`, `dsh-llm-pi-ai`)
- Surface: Web GUI (`dsh web`), `llm-pi-ai` multi-provider adapter
- OS: Windows (platform-independent)

## Reproduction

Preconditions:

- Configure at least two providers under `llm-pi-ai.providers`, e.g.:
  - `opencode-go` with model `deepseek-v4-flash`
  - `bitdeer` with model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`
- The session/agent must be **created while** the effective model is `opencode-go` / `deepseek-v4-flash` (via `agent-default-model` or the session's `/model` selection at creation).

Steps:

1. Create a session (its agent's `options` are stamped with `opencode-go` / `deepseek-v4-flash`).
2. **After** the agent exists, switch the model to `bitdeer` / `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` (composer `/model`, or change `agent-default-model`).
3. Verify the parent's own next requests now use `bitdeer` (visible in the session's `request/header`).
4. Run a `workflow` whose `agent()` calls pass **no** `provider` / `model` override (e.g. `agent(prompt, { label, phase })`).
5. Inspect each spawned subagent's `request/header`.

Actual result: every spawned subagent's `request/header` config is `{ "provider": "opencode-go", "model": "deepseek-v4-flash" }` — the provider captured **at agent creation** — while the parent's own concurrent requests are `{ "provider": "bitdeer", "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash" }`. In the observed session this silently consumed a third-party weekly quota (`429 GoUsageLimitError`, "Weekly usage limit reached").

Expected result: subagents inherit the agent's **current effective model selection** (the same provider/model the parent is actually using for its own requests), or the delegation layer exposes an explicit, documented "subagent default model" that cannot silently diverge from what the user sees.

## Evidence (from the affected session export)

Parent session jsonl (every request, from the first): config is `bitdeer` / `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`.

Sub-agent session jsonl (every child, e.g. `subagents/<id>/session.jsonl`):

```json
{"type":"request/header","data":{"header":{"config":{"provider":"opencode-go","model":"deepseek-v4-flash","maxTokens":384000},...}}}
```

Quota error observed in the same sub-agent:

```
429: {"type":"GoUsageLimitError","message":"Weekly usage limit reached. Resets in 1 day. To continue using this model now, enable usage from your available balance: https://opencode.ai/workspace/<redacted>}"}
```

Parent-session workflow records: `tool-workflow/run-start` × 6, `tool-workflow/agent-start` × 31; the workflow scripts passed only `{ label, phase }` — no `provider`/`model` overrides.

## Code analysis

1. **`agent.options` is a creation-time snapshot that is never rewritten.** `dsh-agent-loop` constructs the agent with the `options` passed at creation (`prepare(ownerCtx, id, options, session)` → `new ReactLoopAgent(loopCtx, id, options, session)` → `this.options = options`). Nothing updates `this.options` when the model is switched.

2. **Per-request model is seeded from `options`, then overridden by a live `selection` without touching `options`** (`dsh-agent-loop`, `ReactLoopAgent.buildRequest`):

   ```js
   const route = { provider: this.options.provider ?? "", model: this.options.model ?? "" };
   const maxTokens = this.options.maxTokens;
   const seedConfig = ... { ...route, ...(reasoningEffort === undefined ? {} : { reasoningEffort }),
                              ...(maxTokens === undefined ? {} : { maxTokens }) };
   const proposedConfig = await this.dispatch.waterfall("agent/request", {...}, () => Promise.resolve(seedConfig));
   ```

   The `agent/request` waterfall is where `installModelSelection` (`dsh-agent/lib/types/model-selection.js`) applies the live per-session selection — so a model switch changes the agent's own requests while `this.options` stays frozen at the creation-time value.

3. **Subagents inherit `parent.options` and never see step 2's override** (`dsh-subagent/lib/types/child-agent.js`, `resolveChildAgentOptions`):

   ```js
   export function resolveChildAgentOptions(parent, requested, childDepth) {
       const parentProvider = parent.options.provider;
       const parentModel = parent.options.model;
       const parentMaxTokens = parent.options.maxTokens;
       return { ...(parentProvider !== undefined ? { provider: parentProvider } : {}),
                ...(parentModel !== undefined ? { model: parentModel } : {}),
                ...(parentMaxTokens !== undefined ? { maxTokens: parentMaxTokens } : {}),
                ...requested, subagentDepth: childDepth };
   }
   ```

4. **The `workflow` engine only overrides when the model-facing call explicitly does so** (`dsh-workflow-worker-thread/lib/index.js`, `startChild`): `agentOptions` is built only when `request.provider` or `request.model` is present; otherwise the child purely inherits step 3.

So the two surfaces — the request-layer `selection` and the delegation-inherited `options` — are deliberately decoupled for live switching, but only one of them updates, turning the decoupling into a silent misroute for every delegated child. There is no guard or warning when a child's inherited provider differs from the parent's current request provider.

## Suggested fixes (any one prevents the silent divergence)

- At delegation time, resolve the child model from the agent's **current effective selection** (the same `selection` `installModelSelection` applies to the parent's requests), instead of the raw `parent.options` snapshot.
- When the session/agent selection changes (via `/model` or `agent-default-model`), also update `agent.options` — or otherwise version the stamp — so delegation inheritance tracks the switch.
- Alternatively, expose a first-class, visible "subagent default model" that defaults to the current selection and is surfaced in the UI/session record, and log a warning when a child resolves to a different provider than the parent's current request route.

## Notes / secondary observation

In the affected deployment the base composition default `agent-default-model` is `deepseek-official` / `deepseek-v4-flash`, but no `llm-deepseek` section is configured, so that route is unserved; the bare model id `deepseek-v4-flash` is offered by `opencode-go` (a pi-ai built-in provider) while other providers use namespaced ids. This makes a misrouted default land on a specific provider quietly. Consider logging a warning whenever a request's provider is resolved from a bare model id across providers, and/or validating that `agent-default-model` points at a configured route at creation.

## Closing notes

No code patch yet — this is a bug report with reproduction, observed evidence, and code-level analysis. Happy to provide sanitized log excerpts or a minimal repro setup on request.

comments.body:
Verified against v0.1.1-rc.2 source — your diagnosis is correct, and the 43-subagent/429-quota observation makes it the strongest evidence yet for a mechanism that has now been independently reported three times. This is the fifth member of a family I have been tracking; the fix blueprint already exists.

**Source confirmation**
- `resolveChildAgentOptions` (`packages/subagent/subagent/src/child-agent.ts:68-83`) copies `parent.options.provider/model/maxTokens` and spreads the per-call override. It reads the *creation-time snapshot*, exactly as you describe.
- `installModelSelection` (`packages/core/agent/src/model-selection.ts:39-78`) registers `system-prompt/assemble` and `agent/request` waterfall handlers on the **parent's scoped ctx**. The child is composed on its own ctx via `ctx.agents.create(...)` (continuation.ts) — it never enters the parent's selections map, so no handler rewrites its route. Your "separate layer only overrides the current agent's own requests" is precisely right.
- Seed timing locks it: `buildRequest` (`agent-loop/src/agent.ts:440-486`) seeds the first `request/header` from `this.options` when `!requestHeaderLogged` — the divergence is decided entirely at seed time.

**Family (5 reports, same root: creation-time snapshot vs live selection)**
- #2904 — subagent auth-401: frozen `parent.options` after a mid-session switch, 100% child dispatch failure with dead credentials.
- #3552 — subagent billing-misroute: same frozen-options mechanism, independent repro, wrong billing account. Root-cause analysis matched yours; I identified the third-layer gap there: the child ctx has no selection slot installed at all (no `agent/request` waterfall, so `buildRequest` always reads frozen options).
- #4077 (this report) — same mechanism, now with the quota-exhaustion consequence (429 GoUsageLimitError). Your parent-log-contains-zero-references-to-opencode-go point is the cleanest discriminator for this class.
- #3565 — compaction summarization: `summarizer.ts` prefers `session.requestHeader()?.config` over the configured target, which can be days stale on resumed sessions → zero cache reuse + wrong-provider billing. Same "last routed header as default" heuristic, same freshness problem.
- #1627/#1703/#2143 — replay-state coherence (truncate/continue mid-tool-call): persisted context vs live metadata diverge, hard-fail the turn.
Common lesson: any "inherit from the parent/persisted artifact" default is sound only while the source is warm; once it can outlive a model switch or a session resume it needs a freshness guard. Fix shape shared across all members: inject the live source over the persisted snapshot.

**Fix blueprint (three tiers, from the earlier analysis)**
1. **Minimal (one call site)**: in `resolveChildAgentOptions`, prefer `parent.session.requestHeader()?.config` over `parent.options` — `requestHeader()` is a public Session API (`session/index.ts:670`) and the module doc notes both the one-shot driver and the continuation manager compose children through this one function, so one change covers `subagent` and `subagent_fork`. There is even a precedent in the same file: `childSessionMeta` (child-agent.ts:102) already reads `parent.session.header` for durable metadata.
2. **Edge case**: a child spawned *immediately after* the switch, before the parent's next request, still sees a stale folded header (the picker's pending selection is not yet in any request/header). Fixing that needs the child to share the parent's live `WebModelSelectionRef` (crosses the api-proxy/subagent boundary), or moving the route decision to the child's first `agent/request` waterfall.
3. **Symmetric long-term**: in-process children share the parent's selection ref so `/model` picker switches propagate too — and keep the two sources aligned (`child-agent.ts:73` inheritance and `agent.ts:440` route construction), otherwise only the descriptor/header first request gets fixed and later steps drift again.

**Blind spot worth checking**: continuable children on cold resume — does the resume path re-resolve the route from the live default, or keep the stale persisted header until the first request? If the latter, the resume path needs the same freshness guard (this is exactly what bit #3565).

One question for your repro: were the workflow subagents spawned through the in-process provider (continuable) or the fork provider? The fork path re-creates the agent from the live default on resume, which would mask the bug in some scenarios — your 43/43 consistency suggests in-process, but confirming pins the fix surface.

This now has a tested alternative route for users who need to stop silent cross-provider delegation immediately. It does not claim to fix DSH's native spawn provider; it runs stock `@tintinweb/pi-subagents` as native DSH child sessions through pi2dsh:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <你的-profile> add pi2dsh
dsh plugin --profile <你的-profile> add @tintinweb/pi-subagents
```

An unpinned child inherits the parent session's last durable real request route, not `agent.options` stamped at creation. Explicit per-child selection still wins. The provider/model pair is persisted in the child's own `request/header`, so billing drift is auditable.

Real acceptance: stock dsh-TUI, parent request on the official route, `/model` switch to an independent gateway, then one unpinned child. Durable logs show the parent on `official → work-gw` and the child on `work-gw` only, followed by a real child tool execution. No screen-text inference is involved.

Reproduction and evidence:
https://github.com/weijiafu14/pi2dsh/tree/main/examples/subagents
https://github.com/weijiafu14/pi2dsh/blob/main/community/subagents-acceptance-report.md

spawn 子代理路由两源拼接：provider 继承父会话、model 落全局默认，多 provider 下产生非法组合（UNKNOWN_MODEL）

建议修复：spawn 解析处改为 pair inheritance；或至少在 UNKNOWN_MODEL 时回退父会话实际模型。

records.title: Feature: opt-in steering delivery ('next-step') for continuable subagents alongside FIFO followup
records.body:
## Summary

Delivery to a continuable background subagent is hardwired to FIFO next-turn queueing through `followup`. There is no way to give a running child mid-turn guidance without destroying its current turn via `interrupt`. Corrections sent through `send_message` (or the GUI subagent prompt) wait until the whole turn finishes, which is too late to change committed work. A long single-turn task cannot be corrected while it runs.

The steering primitive exists at the Agent level, and the product exposes it today for exactly one direction: human input into the root session, through GUI Busy-Enter and the queue dock steer action. This proposal adds an opt-in delivery mode for parent-to-child sends.

## Current behavior

`send_message` calls `ctx.subagents.followup()` and ends at `agent.followup(msg)`, which is `send(msg, 'next-turn', true)`, an append to the FIFO turn queue. The control tool test states the intent directly: "A follow-up is its own later turn, never steering inside the first one."

Locations involved:

- `packages/subagent/subagent/src/continuation.ts`. `submit()` calls `activation.handle.agent.followup(message)` unconditionally inside `admitWaking()`.
- `packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts` lines 122-132. `followup` targets `'next-turn'`, `steer` targets `'next-step'`. Both are waking sends.
- `packages/subagent/tool-subagent-control/src/index.ts`. The schema accepts only `subagent_id` plus `message`.
- `packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts` line 2662. The GUI subagent prompt uses the same `ctx.subagents.followup()` path.
- Precedent for exposing the choice exists in the child-to-parent report channel, where `SubagentReportDelivery` selects `'next-step'` among other presets (`deliverReport`/`sendReport`).

### Live reproduction

A child gets a multi-batch file-writing task ("write numbers 1 to 20"). A correction arrives while it runs ("must not contain 34"):

```
TURN 1   original prompt claimed
         step: write 1-5      correction already queued here
         step: write 6-10     still not read
         step: write 11-15    still not read
         step: write 16-20
         step: DONE_ALL       first look at the inbox happens here
TURN 2   correction claimed   too late to matter
```

The child claims the queued message only after the last step of turn 1, and nothing retracts the numbers already written.

One more limitation: `interrupt_agent` cancels the running turn but keeps parked messages (`keepInbox: true`). A redirect sent after the interrupt runs behind every stale item still queued, because a parent has no way to flush or reorder a child inbox. The GUI queue dock refuses sessions owned by subagents by design.

## Proposal

Add an opt-in delivery mode along the existing seam.

1. Add `SubagentFollowupOptions.delivery?: 'next-turn' | 'next-step'`, defaulting to `'next-turn'` (today's behavior).
2. In `ContinuationManager.submit()`, choose `.steer(message)` or `.followup(message)` from that option. Both are waking sends inside the same `admitWaking()` wrapper, so lifecycle and settlement accounting stays unchanged.
3. Expose the option on `send_message` (tool-subagent-control) and optionally on the GUI `subagents.prompt` RPC.

| Child state | `'next-turn'` (default) | `'next-step'` |
|---|---|---|
| running | waits behind the current turn | consumed at the next step boundary |
| idle | new turn | new turn (same outcome) |

A steered message also lands ahead of items already parked in the queue, so a parent can correct course without flushing anything.

## Concurrency window to design for

Routed through the manager, steering changes no bookkeeping in the common path. A steered send aimed at a child that settles concurrently can still lose against disposal, and disposal clears an unclaimed inbox. Two options: reuse the retry pattern from `followup()` (wait out the disposal transaction, then cold-resume), or document that a lost race degrades to a plain queued message. Both keep the feature no worse than what ships today.

## Alternatives considered

Prompt discipline alone (checkpointed prompting, self-superseding wording) works sometimes, but it depends on model behavior and cannot preempt a long turn. A side plugin calling `ctx.agents.get(id)?.steer(msg)` works today, but it skips `admitWaking()` accounting and leaves the product gap open for everyone else.

## Environment

dsh 0.1.1-rc.2, master checkout. Verified against live in-process continuable children; claim ordering comes from session transcripts. Happy to contribute the reproduction as a test case.

comments.body:
There is a working alternative implementation of exactly this mid-turn correction behavior in the Pi plugin route. It does not modify DSH native `send_message`; `@tintinweb/pi-subagents` exposes `steer_subagent`, and pi2dsh maps its Pi `session.steer()` onto the child DSH Agent's `steer`/`next-step` delivery:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <你的-profile> add pi2dsh
dsh plugin --profile <你的-profile> add @tintinweb/pi-subagents
```

The acceptance is deliberately observable rather than a transcript-only claim. The initial child prompt contains one filename/content, while the later steer message contains a different filename/content that never appears in the spawn prompt. The parent is forbidden from running bash. After the real parent/child model run, only the steer-selected file exists with the steered content, proving the running child received and acted on the correction before completing its original turn.

The bridge also preserves `followUp` as the separate FIFO/next-turn surface, so the two semantics do not collapse into one. This is an alternative product path today, not a claim that the DSH native continuation manager has gained the proposed option.

Reproduction and evidence:
https://github.com/weijiafu14/pi2dsh/tree/main/examples/subagents
https://github.com/weijiafu14/pi2dsh/blob/main/community/subagents-acceptance-report.md
